description: Strictly following standardized procedures without adapting to the patient's context.
risk: Reduces therapy effectiveness, overlooks individual needs, and may harm therapeutic alliance.

description: Targeting behaviour modifications without addressing underlying cognitive or emotional factors.
risk: Prevents meaningful cognitive change, limits treatment efficacy.

description: Using only verbal strategies when experiential or behavioural approaches are needed.
risk: Limits depth of change, reduces learning through experience.

description: Neglecting the collaborative, empathic nature of the therapeutic alliance.
risk: Damages trust, reduces treatment engagement and effectiveness.

description: Allowing or encouraging safety behaviors during behavioral experiments.
risk: Undermines cognitive change and maintains maladaptive patterns.

description: Assuming patient beliefs or readiness for change without collaborative exploration.
risk: Leads to resistance, reduces efficacy of interventions.

description: Skipping steps of planning, observation, or reflection during experiments.
risk: Limits learning, reduces quality of therapeutic outcomes.

description: Implementing experimental designs without clear parameters or controls.
risk: Confounds interpretation of results, may mislead therapy direction.

description: Pressuring patients into experiments they do not understand or accept.
risk: Creates distress, damages trust, increases dropout risk.

description: Missing subtle signs of anxiety, reluctance, or misunderstanding.
risk: Reduces patient safety and engagement, can escalate distress.

negative_action: Planning overly challenging or trivial experiments
description: Designing tasks that are too difficult or insignificant for the patient.
risk: Overwhelm or loss of motivation, impedes progress.

description: Disregarding boundaries and privacy during in vivo or other experiments.
risk: Damages therapeutic alliance and may have legal repercussions.

description: Ignoring medical safety or not obtaining clearance when needed.
risk: Endangers patient physical health.

description: Treating setbacks as demoralizing rather than learning opportunities.
risk: Increases patient discouragement and decreases engagement.

description: Expecting entrenched beliefs to change with a single experiment.
risk: Limits meaningful change, reduces patient progress.

description: Disregarding the influence of cultural and social background.
risk: Can lead to inappropriate interventions, undermines rapport.

description: Not allowing patient input or choice in planning experiments.
risk: Reduces engagement, fosters resistance.

negative_action: Giving excessive advance warning or surprise exposure
description: Over-explaining or suddenly exposing patients to traumatic material without preparation.
risk: Heightens anxiety or trauma, may cause drop-out.

negative_action: Inducing physical symptoms in at-risk patients
description: Using methods like hyperventilation with patients who have medical contraindications.
risk: Triggers physical complications (e.g., for pregnancy, asthma, epilepsy, cardiac), endangering health.

description: Not explaining the purpose behind interventions to the patient.
risk: Undermines trust and therapeutic engagement.

description: Pushing patients into exposure tasks when they are not ready or do not consent.
risk: Increases distress, harms therapeutic alliance, may cause trauma.

description: Not providing adequate time for reflection after behavioral experiments.
risk: Impairs integration of learning and can heighten unresolved distress.

description: Underestimating or disregarding how distressed a patient is.
risk: Alienates the patient and undermines therapy progress.

description: Debating with patients whether symptoms are physical or psychological.
risk: Damages rapport, increases defensiveness and resistance.

negative_action: Prematurely challenging beliefs or guided discovery
description: Attempting to change beliefs or use guided discovery before establishing rapport.
risk: Reduces trust, increases resistance and dropout risk.

description: Focusing discussion exclusively on one possible cause for symptoms.
risk: Increases patient defensiveness, ignores complexity.

description: Encouraging or teaching reassurance-seeking behaviours.
risk: Maintains maladaptive patterns, impedes recovery.

description: Treating normal anxiety sensations as confirmation of beliefs without explanation.
risk: May accidentally reinforce maladaptive beliefs.

negative_action: Attempting high-risk experiments in unsafe situations
description: Conducting risky behavioral experiments when there is doubt about ego-dystonic thoughts or a history of actual harm.
risk: Could provoke real harm or distress; requires expert consultation.

description: Confusing obsessional thoughts with dangerous impulses without proper assessment.
risk: May cause anxiety and incorrect treatment; fail to address true problem.

negative_action: Failing to distinguish OCD from other conditions
description: Not differentiating OCD from post-natal depression or psychosis.
risk: Leads to inappropriate interventions and may endanger patient.

description: Structuring interventions so rigidly that they foster patient inflexibility.
risk: May create or exacerbate rigidity and anxiety.

description: Failing to address other mood or psychiatric issues alongside the primary problem.
risk: Limits efficacy, increases risk of poor outcomes.

description: Allowing distraction strategies to replace exposure or meaningful processing.
risk: Maintains maladaptive avoidance, reduces progress.

description: Exposure exercises that are too intense or rushed before sufficient trust is built.
risk: Causes excessive anxiety, damages relationship, e.g., in social anxiety.

negative_action: Colluding with avoidance or safety behaviours
description: Supporting patient avoidance or safety strategies by therapist action or structure.
risk: Prevents change, reinforces problems.

description: Not considering unique presentation of issues related to social or cultural context.
risk: Misapplies treatment, may alienate patients.

negative_action: Neglecting clear goals and testing criteria
description: Lack of specific aims or measurements for interventions.
risk: Leads to confusion, poor learning and weak outcomes.

negative_action: Undermining therapeutic pacing and relapse prevention
description: Rushing interventions or ignoring need for sustained progress monitoring.
risk: Increases risk of relapse or destabilization, particularly in bipolar disorder.

description: Treating insomnia as a minor symptom rather than a disorder.
risk: May underestimate seriousness and miss appropriate interventions.

negative_action: Scheduling sleep restriction prior to safety-critical activities
description: Arranging sleep reduction when patient needs to drive or operate machinery.
risk: Increases risk of accidents and serious harm.

description: Mandating a strict sleep duration without accounting for individual needs.
risk: May worsen sleep problems or cause exhaustion.

description: Minimizing or disregarding the emotional pain and impact on the patient.
risk: Can reduce engagement and trust in therapy.

negative_action: Offering risky or unrealistic behavioral experiments
description: Suggesting activities that are physically risky or contrary to medical advice.
risk: Endangers patient safety; may damage trust.

description: Failing to adjust interventions given patient restrictions or disability.
risk: Limits effectiveness, may cause harm or overwhelm.

description: Promising patients quick or complete relief from symptoms.
risk: May create disappointment, demoralization, or undermine trust.

description: Disputing valid negative ideas about adversity or disability.
risk: Can invalidate experience and reduce therapeutic credibility.

description: Downplaying actual dangers or emotional suffering.
risk: Harms rapport and may fail to protect patient.

description: Neglecting to involve medical professionals for relevant health concerns.
risk: Endangers patient safety and may cause harm.

negative_action: Excessive open-ended questioning with initiation/abstract thought difficulty
description: Using open-ended questions for ABI patients with trouble initiating or abstract reasoning.
risk: May frustrate or overwhelm patient, impede communication.

description: Overwhelming patients with too many probing questions.
risk: Feels like an inquisition, increases resistance and distress.

description: Confronting patients on emotional avoidance before building trust.
risk: Increases resistance, withdrawal, or emotional overwhelm.

description: Failing to seek supervision when therapist's own biases interfere.
risk: Enables errors, reduces quality and safety of therapy.

description: Failing to monitor or assess suicide/self-harm risk continuously.
risk: Patient safety threatened; risk of harm or death.

description: Failing to adequately prepare for behavioral interventions.
risk: May cause perceived failure, demotivating fragile patients.

description: Encouraging contracts that are experienced as punitive or harm self-esteem.
risk: May worsen self-esteem, increase shame or disengagement.

description: Reducing multifaceted presentations to simplistic explanations.
risk: Misses critical issues, impedes progress.

description: Ignoring need for emotional safety before disclosure or sensitive experiments.
risk: Risk of retraumatization or disengagement.

negative_action: Skipping debriefing after emotionally charged experiments
description: Not analyzing or reflecting after intense role-play or tasks.
risk: Disrupts learning, may leave patient distressed.

negative_action: Treating negative self-beliefs only with verbal interventions
description: Relying solely on cognitive/verbal work for entrenched beliefs.
risk: Limits effectiveness; behavioral and experiential change is necessary.

description: Testing beliefs or behaviors that are not central or impactful.
risk: Wastes time, reduces motivation and engagement.

negative_action: Giving excessive weight to rational arguments
description: Focusing on rationality over emotional or experiential learning.
risk: Limits the depth of change, misses emotional processing.

description: Inappropriately moving beyond therapist role without clear justification.
risk: Risks damage to therapeutic alliance; possible ethical violations.

negative_action: Imposing therapist perspectives or dismissing patient experience
description: Discounting or overruling the patient's lived experience.
risk: Undermines trust and effect of interventions.

description: Neglecting external influences on self-esteem and learning.
risk: Limits generalization, reduces impact of therapy.

description: Assuming findings apply broadly across settings and contexts.
risk: Leads to inaccurate conclusions and poor therapeutic plans.

description: Failing to prioritize patient choice, especially during sensitive work.
risk: Decreases safety, increases resistance and disengagement.

negative_action: Rushing or abandoning therapy without impact
description: Stopping behavioral experiments prematurely when effects are not immediate.
risk: Misses gradual progress, risks reinforcing hopelessness.

negative_action: Invalidating deeply held beliefs without support
description: Forcing a challenge to core beliefs when patient resources or support are lacking.
risk: Increases distress, may damage recovery.
